title: Use dark mode on Hugging Face without logging in
question: How do I use dark mode on Hugging Face?
answer: Logged out, Hugging Face follows your operating system: switch the system or browser to dark and the site turns dark too. Logged in, you can pick a theme in your account settings. The usermods script on this page keeps huggingface.co in its own dark theme for logged-out visitors even when the system is set to light, on model, dataset and Space pages and the rest of the site. It uses the site's built-in dark styles, so nothing looks out of place.
prompt: Make huggingface.co always use its dark theme, even when I'm logged out and my system is in light mode.
details:
Hugging Face styles its dark theme from a `dark` class on the page's root element and sets that class for guests from the system's `prefers-color-scheme`. The script adds the class before the page draws and adds it back if the page removes it, so there is no light flash.

The app inside a Space comes from a separate address and follows its own theme, usually the system setting. The check loads a model page with the browser in light mode and confirms the dark background and light text.

alternatives.title: System dark mode
alternatives.body: Logged out, the site matches your system or browser colour scheme. Set the operating system, or the browser's own appearance setting, to dark.

alternatives.title: Account theme
alternatives.body: Logged in, the theme is an account setting, so it applies wherever you are signed in.

evidence.note: returns "huggingface dark mode"; suggestions: huggingface dark mode | huggingface dark theme | huggingface model list | how to use huggingface models | how to download huggingface model

check.expect: (() => { const bg = getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor.match(/\d+/g).map(Number); const fg = getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.model-card-content, main .prose') || document.querySelector('h1')).color; const c = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d'); c.fillStyle = fg; c.fillRect(0, 0, 1, 1); const [r, g, b] = c.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1).data; return document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark') && bg[0] < 40 && bg[1] < 40 && bg[2] < 40 && r > 150 && g > 150 && b > 150; })()
check.intact: (() => { const h = document.querySelector('h1'); const p = [...document.querySelectorAll('main .prose p, .model-card-content p')].filter((e) => e.checkVisibility()); return !!h && h.checkVisibility() && p.length >= 3; })()
